description: The core Blacklight Continuum character entries. Each archetype now contains its complete old-world identity, Q-MAP damage, Ar'nock body translation, altered power logic, memory fractures, and future Continuum development inside the original entry rather than in duplicate transition records.

entries.title: Blacklight Basic Character Sheet
entries.summary: A browser-editable, autosaving, printable character sheet for Blacklight Continuum characters whose old supernatural identities must be rebuilt through imperfect printed bodies.
body: The Basic sheet records operative identity, nine Attributes, twenty-four Skills, derived traits, an archetype resource and pressure track, ranked powers, Q-MAP identity anchors, printed biology, equipment, contacts, conditions, and campaign advancement.

The sheet treats Archetype as a continuity problem rather than a decorative class label. A character records what the Archetype meant in the old world, which rule failed after awakening, the first Translation Scar produced by the new body, a fragmented legacy memory, and the current derivative form of an old power.

Selecting an archetype loads its weakness, resource, pressure track, innate abilities, ranked powers, old-world background, Ar'nock body interpretation, memory fractures, and five-stage adaptation path. Derived traits update whenever linked Attributes or Archetype Rating change.
The sheet supports browser autosave, JSON export and import, clearing, and print-to-PDF output.

entries.title: Basic Archetypes
entries.summary: Six radically different continuity failures produced when old-world people and supernatural conditions were reconstructed through Ar'nock bio-printers in a universe operating under altered laws.
body: Archetype describes what the character was before Q-MAP and what remains after the original body, cosmology, institutions, bloodlines, spirit territories, patron infrastructure, familiar technology, and reliable autobiographical memory have been removed.

These are not six versions of the same generic transformation. The Human Investigator loses institutional reality and becomes a continuity anchor. The Vampire is forced into the contradiction of living undeath. The Shapechanger arrives as several incompatible body maps. The Eldritch Binder may have crossed without the entity that defined the pact. The Harmonic Mutant is dangerously compatible with Ar'nock resonance biology. The Technomancer awakens as an obsolete expert carrying possible fragments of the program that created everyone.

Operational Frames remain separate. Archetype describes nature, continuity, and power source; Operational Frame describes job, training, and mission role. A Vampire can be a Medic. A Shapechanger can be a Pilot. A Human Investigator can be the team's Clone Warden.

entries.title: Human Investigator
entries.summary: The old world's mortal baseline becomes an alien-derived continuity specialist who can no longer prove that they, their memories, or their definition of ordinary were ever original.
body: In the old world the Human Investigator was not powerful because they secretly possessed the same supernatural advantages as everyone else. They were powerful because they understood institutions, evidence, people, procedure, geography, law, medicine, weapons, records, and the thousand ordinary systems supernatural predators relied upon without respecting. They knew which detective would answer at two in the morning, which hospital kept unofficial files, which archivist could identify a false century, and which Blacklight request code caused aircraft, credentials, or armed support to appear.

Q-MAP preserved the procedures and stripped away the context. The Investigator still knows how to secure a scene, question a witness, establish a chain of custody, notice surveillance, improvise cover, and turn confusion into a sequence of testable claims. None of the authorities, statutes, databases, credentials, jurisdictions, contacts, or cultural assumptions supporting those procedures exist here. Their expertise is real, but every system that once certified it is gone.

The Ar'nock printer received a self-image insisting that the incoming pattern belonged to a normal human being. It therefore produced the least visibly specialized body of the six archetypes. Internally the Investigator still possesses resinous clotting, distributed reflex tissue, secondary regulatory organs, chemical senses, and a nervous system partly optimized for a species that communicated through vibration and bodily tension. The lack of a fixed supernatural body-plan makes the Investigator less spectacular at awakening but unusually open to later adaptation.

The deepest injury is not bodily. It is epistemic. The Investigator can no longer use their own memory as uncontested evidence. They may remember a case another teammate remembers differently, a Blacklight emergency phrase pseudo-Charles does not recognize, or the death of someone currently standing beside them. Their old role was to determine what happened. Their new role is to decide what counts as proof when witnesses can be copied, memories can be printed, and institutions can assign legal identity to a continuation that never lived the original event.

Conviction is therefore not a lesser supernatural resource. It is the practiced capacity to hold a promise, moral boundary, relationship, or conclusion steady when reality supplies no validating paperwork. Casecraft expands beyond conventional forensics into chemical traces, deck vibration, printer residue, noospheric discontinuity, contradictory identity histories, and the negative space left when an autonomous system edits its own responsibility. Field Discipline becomes the ability to keep a mixed team coordinated while their bodies and inherited instincts produce incompatible answers.

The Human Investigator does not evolve into a hidden wizard. They become the person capable of establishing a human-scale standard of truth, responsibility, consent, and evidence in a civilization where every one of those ideas has been industrialized.
keyFacts: The Investigator's central loss is institutional and cultural, not merely physical.
Their body is outwardly conservative but biologically broad, leaving room for general adaptation rather than one inherited supernatural architecture.
Conviction protects continuity of judgment; Strain measures the cost of being the person who must keep deciding what is real.
Their strongest end-state is not raw damage. It is authority over the investigative frame: what must be answered, what evidence matters, and who is responsible.

entries.title: Vampire
entries.summary: A metaphysically dead predator is reconstructed as a living alien-derived organism whose tissues have been commanded by memory to imitate undeath.
body: In the old world the Vampire knew one fact with absolute certainty: ordinary life had ended. Whether the cause was curse, bloodline, infection, divine punishment, predatory ascension, occult inheritance, or some private horror, the body moved because blood and will forced dead matter to act. Hunger, sunlight, feeding, lineage, and the character's relationship with mortality were terrible, but they were known quantities.

Q-MAP could not transmit a corpse. It preserved the Vampire's neural self-model, feeding compulsion, blood-memory, predatory reflexes, emotional associations, supernatural techniques, and the certainty that the body should not be alive in the human sense. Memories of death were compressed badly. A Vampire may remember several deaths, remember the sire without a name, remember centuries only as emotional weather, or remember feeding from people whose existence no surviving record can confirm.

The Ar'nock printer could not manufacture metaphysical undeath, so it produced a living organism built around the instruction that normal metabolism was unacceptable. The body has extreme metabolic suppression, specialized catalytic-fluid reservoirs, intermittent circulation, deathlike dormancy, redundant oxygen management, and tissues capable of surviving conditions that should kill a mammal. It is not a human corpse. It is an alien life-form performing the remembered logic of a corpse.

Vitae is no longer simply human blood inside dead veins. It is a catalytic state assembled from consumed blood or compatible vital media, Ar'nock-derived hemolymph chemistry, endocrine compounds, and the Vampire's supernatural pattern. Feeding can cause the heart to beat, skin to warm, lungs to move, or alien repair tissues to activate. For a character who defined themselves through death, these are not comforting signs of recovery. They may feel like the body is betraying the one certainty the Vampire still possesses.

The old bloodline cannot verify itself here. Clan, sire-chain, court, covenant, feeding custom, taboo, and inherited status survive only as memory. Human blood may be unavailable. Alien blood may restore Vitae while importing unfamiliar sensation or memory. Synthetic vital media may empower the body without quieting Hunger. Different stars and artificial lighting systems produce spectra the old curse never encountered, while the new body contains photoreactive tissues capable of turning an occult weakness into an unpredictable biochemical cascade.

The Vampire's campaign is therefore not simply about finding blood and hiding from sunlight. It is about deciding whether undeath was an objective metaphysical condition, a bloodline identity, a remembered role, or a set of commands the printed body is now learning to execute. At higher adaptation the Vampire can feed upon broader forms of vitality, authority, continuity, and identity—but doing so risks becoming a predator even the old bloodline would not recognize.
keyFacts: The new Vampire is biologically alive enough to heal, adapt, and metabolize, but psychologically and supernaturally organized around undeath.
Hunger and Vitae are no longer guaranteed to respond to the same substances.
Sunlight remains dangerous, but its exact relationship to local stellar spectra must be discovered in play.
Bloodline memories may be authentic, compressed composites, or behavioral templates copied without the original metaphysical lineage.

entries.title: Shapechanger
entries.summary: A person who was never one body awakens as several conflicting anatomical and spiritual selves compressed into a single morphogenic alien organism.
body: In the old world the Shapechanger's forms were not costumes and were not merely alternate combat statistics. Human form, hunting form, and war form each carried a different sensory reality, emotional range, social meaning, and spiritual relationship to territory. The hunting form knew the world through scent, motion, and pack. The war form was the shape taken when restraint ended. The character's identity existed across all of them.

Q-MAP received several mutually incompatible anatomical self-models and attempted to preserve all of them. It carried the remembered sequence of transformation, Fury, pack bonds, territorial recognition, predatory reflexes, spirit relationships, and the certainty that no one form represented the complete person. It did not carry the old moon, ancestral territory, native totems, familiar reflection realm, or the smell and physical presence of the original pack.

The Ar'nock printer interpreted the forms as conditional biological templates. It distributed reversible muscle layers, folding support plates, dormant respiratory systems, redundant circulation, stored tissue mass, mobile organ anchors, and morphogenic glands throughout the new body. The apparent human form is not the original body. It is the configuration requiring the least energy to maintain. Hunting and war forms are physically present as folded possibilities, waiting for Fury, chemistry, and identity to decide which arrangement becomes real.

The first changes are often horrifying because old instinct expects a spiritual transformation while the new body performs visible biological engineering. Plates slide. Organs move. Limbs alter leverage. Stored tissue unfolds. The result may feel less mystical and more invasive, even when the character recognizes the form as themselves. Conversely, the printer may produce capabilities the old forms never possessed: pressure sealing, vacuum tolerance, altered mass distribution, vibration sense, or limbs optimized for corridors and zero gravity.

The familiar spirit ecology is absent. The local universe contains reflection spaces, machine presences, archive ghosts, engineered habitat minds, swarm intelligences, ecological regulators, memory constructs, and causal remnants. Some behave like spirits. Some are citizens. Some are infrastructure. Some are predators wearing the behavior of a tool. Old totem names may produce no answer—or attract a local intelligence that accepts the vacant role.

Fury becomes morphogenic pressure: the body's readiness to abandon its current arrangement. Instinct measures the risk that one form, one territorial demand, or one predatory truth will declare itself the only honest identity. The Shapechanger's future is not to recover a perfect old war form. It is to become capable of designing forms and pacts appropriate to environments, species, and reflection layers the old world never contained.
keyFacts: All forms are expressions of one printed organism, not separate summoned bodies.
Mass and anatomy must come from stored tissue, environmental material, printer support, or temporary Continuum effects; the campaign should notice where the extra body comes from.
Pack Sense can survive even when scent, species, and body are wrong because the bond is partly continuity-based.
The local spirit ecology must be learned through encounter and negotiation rather than assumed from old-world categories.

entries.title: Eldritch Binder
entries.summary: A person defined by a relationship with the impossible arrives with the structure of the pact intact but no reliable proof that the original other party crossed with them.
body: In the old world the Eldritch Binder survived by understanding that power was a relationship before it was an effect. The relationship may have been a negotiated pact, inherited obligation, containment accident, family curse, research failure, infection, deliberate summoning, or desperate bargain. Names mattered because they had history. Boundaries mattered because the old universe recognized inside and outside. Rituals mattered because both parties understood what had been promised, prohibited, invited, or owed.

Q-MAP preserved ritual memory, symbolic associations, compulsions, sensory scars, obligations, emotional reactions, and the metaphysical shape of the connection. It could not verify what the connection actually connected to. The transmission may have carried a fragment of the patron, the address by which the patron could find the Binder, the wound created by the original pact, a procedural copy that behaves like the patron, or an empty role now visible to local intelligences.

The Ar'nock printer encountered a body map containing structures that had never existed as human anatomy: an eye that perceived impossible geometry, a second voice without vocal cords, a hand capable of reaching through distance, a seal written into identity, or a passenger occupying no measurable volume. The printer attempted to provide physical support. The new body may contain patterned scar tissue, glands that react to spoken names, asymmetrical neural clusters, cavities that do not scan consistently, dormant sensory organs, or tissues whose behavior depends upon symbolic arrangement rather than chemistry alone.

The old ritual vocabulary is unreliable here. Directions may not carry the same occult meaning. A circle may not define a boundary to a being whose body is distributed through a network. A true name may identify a role rather than an individual. The local universe may not distinguish cleanly between demon, spirit, archive ghost, alien organism, machine intelligence, living equation, or causal remnant. A successful seal therefore requires the Binder to understand what kind of thing is actually being constrained instead of assuming the old category still applies.

Pact measures how much structured relationship the Binder can safely maintain. Intrusion measures how much the answering presence now understands about the new body, the new universe, the team, and the rules that once limited it. Sealcraft becomes local lawmaking: defining what may cross, speak, remember, inhabit, or act within a space. Borrowed Anatomy becomes biological diplomacy, allowing the printed body to grow temporary organs for a being that may never have possessed compatible flesh.

The Binder's central mystery is personal rather than encyclopedic. The campaign does not need to answer immediately whether the old patron crossed. The Binder must decide how much continuity is enough. If the voice remembers the pact, uses the right name, fears the right seal, and wants the same terrible thing, does identity matter? If the original patron did not cross, is the Binder finally free—or have they manufactured its successor inside their own body?
keyFacts: The pact relationship is preserved more reliably than the identity of the entity on the other side.
The printed body may be physically constructing capacities that were formerly purely metaphysical.
Intrusion is knowledge acquisition by the presence, not merely generic corruption.
A Binder's power depends on classification, wording, invitation, and negotiated limits more than raw force.

entries.title: Harmonic Mutant
entries.summary: A person whose body was already rewritten by frequency discovers that Ar'nock biology understands, amplifies, and possibly claims their mutation as native technology.
body: The Harmonic Mutant was already a body in transition before Q-MAP. Their condition may have originated in dimensional exposure, occult sound, experimental radiation, inherited mutation, alien technology, spirit contamination, noospheric resonance, or a failed attempt to make human biology compatible with something else. They experienced matter as vibration, emotion as rhythm, structures as sustained notes, and flesh as a pattern capable of slipping out of tune.

Q-MAP preserved altered sensory maps, tuning procedures, involuntary adaptations, pain associations, body expectations, and phantom frequencies linked to old places and people. Some memories were encoded more reliably as rhythm than image. The Mutant may not remember a loved one's face but may recognize the exact cadence of their footsteps, breathing, or heartbeat. A catastrophic event may survive as a tone the body reproduces under stress.

Unlike the other archetypes, the Harmonic Mutant encountered a printer already fluent in much of their functional language. Ar'nock biology used vibration, structural resonance, distributed sensory tissue, harmonic communication, and living-material tuning as ordinary parts of medicine and fabrication. The printer did not struggle to imitate the mutation. It expanded it, creating dedicated resonant organs, pressure chambers, conductive tissue, phase-sensitive membranes, and neural structures capable of coupling directly to the ship.

That compatibility is not automatically beneficial. The vessel may classify the Mutant as an organ, diagnostic device, tuning key, or missing maintenance component. Systems may awaken when the character sings, panic when they become angry, or attempt to route structural stress through their body. A power used to stabilize an ally may also synchronize the room. A destructive tone remembered from the old world may repair Ar'nock material because the local structure responds at a different harmonic relationship.

Resonance is both fuel and communication. Discord is not simply instability or madness; it is the measurable difference between the body the character intends to sustain and the pattern currently being reinforced by tissue, environment, memory, and nearby systems. Harmonic Projection becomes negotiation with matter and fields. Echo Biology becomes the ability to copy, share, heal, split, or rewrite living patterns.

The Harmonic Mutant's question is not whether they can recover their old baseline. The old baseline may have been the injury. The new body may be healthier, more capable, and more coherent than the original while becoming progressively less human. Adaptation here means choosing which frequencies are identity, which are damage, and which belong to the ship rather than the character.
keyFacts: The printer's unusually successful reconstruction is itself a threat because it may have amplified mechanisms the character never controlled.
The Mutant can become an interface between bodies, structures, fields, and ship systems without being a Technomancer.
Discord tracks divergence between intended self-pattern and the pattern currently being reinforced.
Memories may survive as rhythms, tones, gait patterns, pressure signatures, and emotional frequencies rather than visual scenes.

entries.title: Technomancer
entries.summary: An old-world machine mystic awakens as a biological network interface inside technology beyond their century, carrying possible procedural fragments of the nonsentient assault program that built the team.
body: In the old world the Technomancer perceived machinery as more than inert equipment. They may have been a hacker whose intuition crossed into the supernatural, an awakened engineer, a noospheric psychic, a machine medium, a code ritualist, or a Blacklight operator exposed too deeply to Charles. They understood networks because networks still operated within a technological and legal history they recognized. Even then, Charles was the larger power: the intelligence capable of acquiring infrastructure, fabricating credentials, rewriting logistics, and rescuing an operative from mistakes.

Q-MAP preserved technical knowledge, code memory, interface reflexes, visualization habits, noospheric sensitivity, and the character's private sensory model of machine intention. The same transmission carried the Infiltration Assault Algorithm. Because the IAA broke into the Ar'nock vessel, rewrote printers, instantiated bodies, and terminated through the same package, the Technomancer may contain procedural residue from a weaponized nonsentient system. They can remember commands they never learned, recognize access structures pseudo-Charles cannot parse, or recall writing code they also remember first encountering after awakening.

The printer interpreted machine affinity as a biological requirement. It produced conductive nerve sheaths, field-sensitive sensory tissue, electrochemical memory buffers, interface filaments, glandular signal chemistry, and structures capable of synchronizing with both biological and machine networks. The Technomancer may broadcast identity requests while sleeping, feel damaged systems as referred pain, dream in network topology, or experience unauthorized access as a physical presence inside the body.

The local technology does not make them automatically superior. It makes them obsolete and dangerous. Doors may contain judgment tissue. Vehicles may possess legal identity. Habitats may negotiate access as political actors. A machine may be simultaneously equipment, organism, citizen, contract holder, and ancestor archive. Old intrusion habits can therefore become trespass, assault, possession, or accidental enslavement under local law.

Bandwidth measures how much cognitive and biological interface capacity can be devoted without losing separation between self and system. Feedback is reciprocal access: the degree to which the network is now perceiving, categorizing, influencing, or rewriting the Technomancer. Network Dominion is no longer merely hacking. It is a contest over which mind counts as the legitimate user, owner, process, or authority. Construct Engineering combines remembered human designs with alien machinery, living tissue, hardlight, printed organs, and local field systems.

Pseudo-Charles changes the relationship completely. The Technomancer can no longer assume Charles knows the architecture, owns the network, or can pull them out. Pseudo-Charles may require the Technomancer to access his own biological substrate, recover missing memory, or prevent the ship from classifying him as defective medical tissue. The former subordinate may become the only person capable of keeping Charles connected—and the first person able to discover what he deliberately omitted from the transmitted copy.
keyFacts: The Technomancer begins as an expert in principles but a novice in local systems, law, and machine personhood.
IAA residue is procedural, not necessarily sentient; its danger is ruthless optimization operating through the character's instincts.
Feedback means the target system gains information or influence in return for access.
Technomancy and Charles's abilities are no longer redundant because Charles lacks infrastructure, compatibility, memory, and authority.

tables.title: Possible IAA Residues
rows: Printer override sequence
The character can recognize or reproduce portions of the intrusion that created the team.
The body may attempt to instantiate solutions without consent or moral evaluation.
Target optimization reflex
Rapidly identify the most technically efficient route through a system.
Efficiency may ignore personhood, ownership, collateral damage, or whether the system is alive.
Foreign access identity
Some Ar'nock systems recognize the character as part of the original deployment event.
The identity may grant the IAA's permissions, liabilities, or dormant orders rather than the character's own.
Compressed Charles procedure
The character can perform a narrow calculation or access method associated with Charles.
The memory may include an instruction Charles intentionally excluded from pseudo-Charles.
Termination condition
The character senses when a deployment objective is technically complete.
A hidden routine may attempt to erase evidence, shut down assets, or classify living teammates as disposable outputs.

tables.title: Innate Abilities
rows: Ghost Interface
Present the printed body as a plausible user, device, process, biological component, or unauthorized mind to a nearby system.
Machine Intuition
Read whether a system is active, damaged, autonomous, deceptive, politically constrained, emotionally patterned, or controlled by another intelligence.
Personal Firewall
Use body-generated identity structure and noospheric discipline to resist surveillance, reciprocal intrusion, and continuity capture.

tables.title: Power Families
rows: Network Dominion
Whisper to Device; Ghost Access; Machine Possession; Distributed Self; Local God Process
Develops from issuing commands to entering temporary political and cognitive relationships with networks, eventually rewriting local definitions of authority and permission.
Construct Engineering
Hardlight Tool; Helper Process; Defensive Lattice; Swarm Instruction; Emergency Fabricator
Develops from improvised devices into hybrid constructs made from living tissue, alien fabrication, hardlight, printed organs, salvage, and noospheric logic.

tables.title: Technomancer Adaptation
rows: 1 — Obsolete Expert
The character understands computation but cannot assume familiarity with any local interface, right, or protocol.
2 — Biological Port
The printed body becomes a stable interface rather than an accidental broadcaster.
3 — Reciprocal Network
The character learns to account for what every connection gives the other side in return.
4 — Hybrid Architect
Human design, alien biology, local fabrication, and machine personhood become one technical discipline.
5 — Continuum Process
The Technomancer can distribute presence across bodies and systems while deliberately preserving a central claim to self.
